title: fix(plugin-approvals): the approval request page's highlights strip names the flow by its label
body:
Fixes #24264

Clause-②: no

The served `sys_approval_request_detail` record page's highlights strip now names the flow by its label, `process_label` (the "Flow" field). Before, it listed the machine source `process_name`, so its first chip read like `flow:deal_desk`. The object's `highlightFields` makes the same swap: `process_label` takes the place of `process_name`, and `record_id` stays on the object's list and off the strip.

Responsibility: `plugin-approvals`' own declarations (the page's highlights `fields` and the object's `highlightFields`) | the platform path already serves the flow label: `process_label` is declared on the object, served by the approvals get, and read by the record title's formula and every request list | reached by every user who opens a served approval request record page.

## The choice: object-level, not page-only

Readings are against objectstack `53ef75243` and objectui at the console pin `.objectui-sha` = `5e15928b4`, by `git show` and `git grep`. The page was not driven in a browser.

**The page's own Details tab reads the object's list, so a page-only edit is not page-only.** The Details tab is a `record:details` node with neither `sections` nor `fields`. The spec declares what such a node draws (`RecordDetailsProps`, `packages/spec/src/ui/component.zod.ts`): the object's `highlightFields`. At the pin, objectui's `record-details.tsx` (objectui#12433) draws that list minus every field the mounted strip registers and minus the H1 field. Its pin `record-details.highlightFieldsFallback-12433.test.tsx` names this page as the case it was built for. So the Details tab is the object's list minus the strip:

| | strip | Details tab |
|---|---|---|
| `main` today | `process_name`, `object_name`, `status`, `current_step`, `submitter_id`, `updated_at` | `record_id` (the target record card) |
| page-only | `process_label`, … | `process_name`, `record_id`: a "Source: flow:NAME" row appears in the tab |
| object-level (this PR) | `process_label`, … | `record_id`, unchanged |

The page's header slot falls through to the synthesizer. Since the page authors `highlights`, the synthesizer's derived strip and `record:path` are not emitted (`buildDefaultPageSchema`'s highlights branch), so the header reads nothing from this list.

**Other readers of the object's `highlightFields`, and whether a request surface reaches them today:**

- `ObjectView` / `ObjectGrid` default columns: used only by a list view that declares no `columns`. All four `sys_approval_request` list views declare columns, and every one already lists `process_label`. Not reached.
- `InterfaceListPage` default columns, `ObjectKanban` default card fields, and `RelatedList` default columns and picker: no interface page, kanban view or related list of requests is declared in this repository. Not reached.
- `LookupField` dropdown preview columns (`deriveLookupColumns`): the two lookups to a request, `sys_approval_action.request_id` and `sys_approval_approver.request_id`, sit on objects whose `enable.apiMethods` is `['get', 'list']`, so no create or edit form opens that picker. Not reached. The Action History list's request cell draws the request's title, not this list.
- `RecordPreviewCard`, the pointer card a `referenceVia` pair draws: reached only where a pointer pair names a request row, for example an audit or activity row about a request. Whether such rows exist is NOT MEASURED. Where they do, the card shows the Flow label where it showed the Source.
- Studio's object settings panel shows the list as authored, now with `process_label`.
- Backend readers: `@objectstack/lint` (field references and semantic roles), `metadata-core`'s field-security fold of the served schema, and `metadata-protocol`'s build probes. None of these changes behaviour for a list of existing fields. The page test's build-rule leg stays green.

objectui's console served-page pin copies (`apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.servedPage*.test.tsx` at the pin) copy both lists with `process_name`. objectstack-ai/objectui#12484 rewrites them, and they are not touched here.

## The null case, within declared fields

The console reads a request through the approvals get (`routeApprovalRecordReads`, `apps/console/src/AppContent.tsx` at the pin). There, `rowFromRequest` serves `process_label` by the one chain in `display-labels.ts` (`requestDisplayLabels`): the stored label, else the node-config snapshot's `__flowLabel`, else `process_name` humanized (`flow:deal_desk` becomes `Deal Desk`). `approval-service.test.ts` pins that fallback ("rows fall back to prettified machine names when labels are absent"). What a user sees:

- **A label is stored, or the snapshot carries one:** the Flow chip shows the flow's authored label.
- **No label stored** (a row written before the column, before or after a failed boot fill): the Flow chip shows the humanized machine name, never `flow:NAME`.
- **The chain yields nothing:** this needs a `process_name` that humanizes to nothing (`flow:` followed by nothing), and `openNodeRequest` never writes one (it writes `flow:` plus the flow name or the node id). The field then has no value, and the console's strip draws no chip for a field with no value in read mode, so there is no Flow chip. The record title still names `process_name`: on the approvals get through `titleFormat`, since that get serves no `display_title`, and on the data API through `display_title`'s fallback.
- **The same record read through the generic data API** (a host without the console's routing): `process_label` is the stored column, null on a row the boot fill has not labelled. The chip is then absent, and `display_title` reads `process_name · record_id`.

No other field fills the chip. No field, formula or column is added, and there is no spec row: `record:highlights` `fields` already admits the field.

## Tests (at `046ca5b66`)

- `pnpm --filter '@objectstack/plugin-approvals^...' build`: VERDICT command-exit 0. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals build`: exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/sys-approval-request-page.test.ts src/sys-approval-request.object.test.ts src/sys-approval-display-title.test.ts`: 3 files, 36 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals test`: `Test Files 81 passed (81)`, `Tests 1108 passed (1108)`. The package has 81 test files.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck`: exit 0, with `check:test-typecheck: OK`.
- The pin `sys-approval-request-page.test.ts` moves. Its existing case still holds the strip to the object's list minus `record_id`. A new case asserts three things: both lists lead with `process_label`, neither lists `process_name`, and the object's list minus the strip is exactly `record_id` (the Details tab).

**Ablation (one run, then restored).** `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` put `process_name` back at the head of the page's strip. Its on-disk evidence: anchor x1 → x0, replacement x0 → x1, blob `aea7e3212b97` → `822555700a37`. The pin went red: `Tests 2 failed | 15 passed (17)`. The new case failed with `expected 'process_name' to be 'process_label'`, and the existing case failed on the strip no longer equalling the object's list minus `record_id`. The restore leg: blob after restore == HEAD (`aea7e3212b97`), `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status` clean. No test file is left behind by the ablation.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `046ca5b66` derived 67 commands for this diff. All 67 ran locally at `046ca5b66`, each exit code captured before any pipe:

- 65 exited 0 on the first pass.
- Two first refused with exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET: `pnpm check:i18n` (the CLI was not built) and `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (packages without `dist/`). After the prerequisite builds (the i18n gate's own one-command closure, then `turbo run build --filter=!@objectstack/docs`), both exited 0. `check-i18n-bundles: OK (10 package(s) — all bundles in sync, no undeclared authoring keys)`; `✓ check:dual-build-cjs-loads — 111 published require entry point(s) across 69 package(s) load`.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` reconciliation: `67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`.

The repo-wide scans (`pnpm lint` and the rest of the CI battery) are CI's. Their PR check-runs are the reading.

## Acceptance notes

- Out of scope, reported to the seat and left as it is: the strip's Current Step chip draws `current_step`, the Approval node's machine id (`openNodeRequest` writes `current_step: input.nodeId`, and `rowFromRequest` serves it as written). It is the same machine-name shape. Swapping in `current_step_label` the same way would draw nothing on the served page, because the approvals get serves the step label as `step_label`, not under the column's name.
- The served page's H1 reads `flow:NAME · ID` on the approvals get, which serves no `display_title`. objectstack-ai/objectui#12484 carries the H1 (the face 5 fit-check reading `6246163097` on objectstack-ai/objectui#12491). This PR does not touch it.
- The page header's tabs bullet said the Details tab holds "the request's own fields by the object's field groups". At the pin it draws the object's `highlightFields` minus the strip, which is `record_id` only. The same header edit corrects it.
